Resolves #18617

Refs #18605

The rule this enforces: **a class extension never replaces a class field with a config, or a config with a field.** A field is an own data property initialized by `new`; a config is a prototype value or, when reactive, a prototype accessor generated by `Neo.setupClass`; a name shared across the two in one prototype chain is a collision, not an override — the own property shadows the prototype for reads and writes alike, so a plain config's value never applies and a reactive config's `beforeSet` / `afterSet` never run (measured below). `Neo.createConfig` already refuses the setter flavour of the same rule at setup time; it cannot see fields, which exist only after `new`. `Neo.create` now refuses the field flavour right after `new cls()` and before `construct(config)`: at that seam all class fields have been initialized and no construct() has run, so an own **data** property whose key is an own key of the merged static config (`Object.hasOwn(cls.config, key)`) is the collision, for plain and reactive configs alike, and it throws the way the setup-time guard does — naming the field, the instance class and, for a reactive config, the class whose accessor it shadows and the hook that would never fire. Own accessors are ordinary overrides and pass; a `construct()` that assigns a plain config before `super.construct()` runs after the check and passes; and there is no per-class cache, because a custom native constructor may shape an instance, so the diagnostic describes what it observes after native construction.

`Decision Record impact: none`.

Evidence: unit tier (the class system in the Node unit runtime; the full tier constructs every engine, app and example class the suites touch) → unit tier required. Residual: none.

## Deltas from ticket

The agreed boundary is now immediately after native construction in `Neo.create`, before `construct(config)`. The predicate checks own data properties against own keys of the merged static config, covering plain and reactive configs. The old Base.construct invocation and per-class cache are absent. A subclass cannot legalize a conflicting declaration by deleting the field later in construct(); ordinary assignments made there remain valid. The ticket ledger has been reconciled with the author's adopted placement and the operator's rule.

## What does not work without the change
Measured on unmodified `dev@8cab26fcf8` (no guard), with a base class declaring the field `value = null`, a subclass declaring `value_: 1` with an `afterSetValue` counter, and a control class declaring only `value_: 1`:

| Step | Control (config only) | Shadowed (base field + subclass config) |
|---|---|---|
| after `Neo.create` | `value` 1, hook fired once | `value` null, hook never fired — own data property present, `isConfig('value')` true |
| `set({value: 3})` | 3, hook twice | 3, hook never |
| `instance.value = 5` | 5, hook three times | 5, hook never |
| `observeConfig(instance, 'value', fn)` then `value = 7` | fires | fires zero times |
| `delete instance.value; instance.value = 9` | — | 9, hook fires once: the accessor was there all along |

The order is the documented one (`learn/guides/fundamentals/InstanceLifecycle.md` §1 step 1: `new YourClass()` initializes every class field before `construct()` runs), and the order is exactly what produces the collision: the field becomes an own data property, the subclass's generated accessor for `value_` lives on the prototype, and an own data property shadows a prototype accessor for reads and writes alike. `processConfigs` then skips the initial assignment because the instance already owns the key (the `hasOwnProperty` branch meant for non-reactive configs), and every later write lands in the field. For the instance's lifetime the reactive config is dead — no default, no `beforeSet` / `afterSet`, no `observeConfig`, no binding — and nothing reports it. The guides document the order, not the collision; `Neo.createConfig` catches the same-name conflict at setup time only when it is a setter, never a field. The origin was `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace`'s `dockModel = null` field against a subclass declaring `dockModel_` (D#18594's ShadowWorkspace receipt): `afterSetDockModel` never ran, and nothing said why.

## Cost — benchmarked
The maintainer asked for the guard's cost against creating many instances, nested trees and config-heavy classes alike. `test/playwright/unit/core/FieldConfigGuardProfile.spec.mjs` (eab27d3cb6) pins it in the unit runtime: interleaved construction samples with the guard live and stubbed, the first arm alternating per pair, then the guard alone on the exact after-new shapes it inspects.

| Shape | Instances per sample | Construction per instance | Guard live vs stubbed | Guard alone | Guard's share of one instance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A container of 60 toolbars × 5 buttons (layouts included) | 422 | ~155 µs | 2.2 % (sampling noise; −0.06 % on a 1201-instance run) | 151 ns on `new Button()` — 5 own properties, 83 configs | 0.10 % |
| A grid over 200 records × 12 columns | 44 | ~212 µs | 0.17 % (1.0 % creation-only in a 30-pair run) | 230 ns on `new GridContainer()` — 9 own properties, 97 configs | 0.11 % |
| Synthetic: 200 configs over 4 fields · 200 configs over 30 fields · 5 configs over 30 fields | — | — | — | 129 · 847 · 880 ns | — |

The guard walks the instance's own class fields (private `#` fields are not own property names; a Component owns four, a grid container nine) and probes `cls.config` once per name, so its cost follows fields at roughly 27 ns each and ignores the size of `static config`. Ceilings in the spec: a tenth of construction for the interleaved arms; one percent of an instance, 1 µs for 200 configs over 4 fields and 5 µs over 30 fields for the guard alone; and the 4-field/200-config class cheaper than the 30-field/5-config one.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] None: the guard has no post-merge-only effect.

## Decision
The rule is written where an extension author reads it — `learn/guides/fundamentals/ExtendingNeoClasses.md` §2 ("Fields and configs never trade places", beside the redeclared-config rule) and `core.Base`'s static-config docblock beside its "vs. Class Fields" paragraph — and the engine enforces it in full at the one seam where it is clean. The seam was measured, not chosen: the four-crossings predicate at the top of `Base#construct` fired on every component (1864 throws across the tier), because `component.Base#construct` clones `_vdom` onto the instance before `super.construct()` and `_vdom` is a declared config key — a legitimate pre-super assignment, not an authoring error. The same predicate right after `new cls()` in `Neo.create`, where no `construct()` has run, passes the whole tier with zero throws from any engine, app or example class. @neo-gpt's convergence proposal on #18617 named that seam and the four crossings; the disposition on the ticket records the adoption. Every `static config` class is created through `Neo.create` (singletons included, via `setupClass`); the direct `new` sites in `src` are plain helper classes without a static config.

## Evolution
Round 1 placed the check at the top of `Base#construct` with a per-class cache; the review measured an own accessor refused as a config and a clean first instance exempting a later shadowed one. Round 2 narrowed the predicate to reactive configs and dropped the cache. The maintainer then stated the rule the check exists for — never trade a field for a config or vice versa — and the reviewer's counter-control showed the construct seam was what kept the plain half out of reach. Round 3 moves the check to the creation seam and enforces the rule in full. Round 4 adds the profile the maintainer asked for; the engine change is untouched since 2fa73d6e73.

### `@neo-gpt` commented on 2026-09-12T21:50:30Z

[MERGE_HOLD]

I am suspending my approval at `c401bd9f64659903169b1a29d4edc0858bd43635` following the operator's clarification of the premise:

> a class extension should NEVER replace a class field with a class config or vice versa.

The inherited property category is fixed. Changing a field's value or a config's default within its category is a different operation from reclassifying that property in a subclass.

My first review became a review of accessor-shadow detection; Round 2 correctly verified its two repairs. That did not settle the prior question: whether the class system needs additional per-instance machinery to diagnose this invalid inheritance declaration. Native own-property shadowing in the ticket's example is not evidence that `Neo.create`, `construct`, or fields-first `set()` initializes valid extensions incorrectly.

The boundary is also broader than `isConfig()`'s reactive category: an exact-head probe accepts both base field → subclass non-reactive config and base non-reactive config → subclass field, as well as valid field → field and config → config controls. This observation distinguishes the proposed reactive-shadow diagnostic from the operator's inheritance rule; it does **not** prescribe expanding the runtime guard.

The ticket's justification and intended enforcement boundary need revalidation before my approval can be used for merge. The R1/R2 repairs remain technically verified. No new implementation direction is authorized by this note.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — [P1] Ordinary accessors are rejected as reactive configs.** At [Base:1131](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/a370c4bf8380935295671eefa5591b3bf94acc6b/src/core/Base.mjs#L1131), `Object.keys(me)` includes enumerable own accessors installed by an overriding `construct()`, and `hasPropertySetter` accepts any setter, including that very own accessor. No own-data-descriptor check or config-membership check occurs. A class with only `factor_: 2` and this documented pre-super initialization works on parent `b73cafba`:

```js
construct(config) {
    let value = 0;
    Object.defineProperty(this, 'value', {
        enumerable: true, configurable: true,
        get() { return value },
        set(next) { value = next * this.factor }
    });
    super.construct(config)
}
```

After creation, `instance.set({value: 3, factor: 4})` yields `value === 12`, with `isConfig('value') === false`. This head throws before construction, claiming `value_` was “declared by undefined.” A second control — a subclass's plain `value = 5` overriding a parent's ordinary `get/set value`, with no config named `value` — also newly throws. [Base#isConfig](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/a370c4bf8380935295671eefa5591b3bf94acc6b/src/core/Base.mjs#L726) and [Base#set](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/a370c4bf8380935295671eefa5591b3bf94acc6b/src/core/Base.mjs#L1075) already distinguish these categories.

**Challenge — [P2] A clean first instance suppresses later real collisions.** At [Base:1129](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/a370c4bf8380935295671eefa5591b3bf94acc6b/src/core/Base.mjs#L1129), memoization certifies the constructor from the first instance's keys. Those keys have already passed through subclass `construct()` pre-processing. With `value_: 1`, `value = null`, and:

```js
construct(config = {}) {
    if (config.unmask) delete this.value;
    super.construct(config)
}
```

Creating `{unmask: true}` first produces `value: 1, hookCalls: 1` and caches the class. The next ordinary instance retains the shadow, accepts `set({value: 3})`, and reports `hookCalls: 0` without an error. Validation must not depend on which config created the first instance.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit:** The ordering documentation is correct. “Object.keys(instance) is exactly the class fields” is not: subclass pre-processing precedes this base hook. “No false positives” is bounded by the tested population, which misses both non-config controls above.

**Findings:** Two delivered-scope correctness defects.

* **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: A guard over every Base construction must preserve the native accessor/non-config distinction that Base already exposes.
